newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila Central Bank says trade deficit manageable.
newsitem.headline: Manila Central Bank says trade deficit manageable.

text.p: Central Bank Governor Gabriel Singson said on Tuesday the country's trade deficit situation remained under control and that the trend is consistent with a growing economy.

In a speech to businessmen, Singson said "we are convinced the situation remains well in hand. The underlying merchandise trade deficit is quite manageable and consistent with a healthily growing economy."

The country's trade deficit, which widened to $7.133 billion in the first seven months of 1996 versus $4.876 billion in the 1995 period, had been a cause of concern. The Asian Development Bank, in a recent report, had said the appreciation of the peso could have put further pressure on the trade balance.

Singson said though export growth had slowed down to over 19 percent from last year's 30 percent, the country posted faster export growth than the rest of Asia compared to Hong Kong's 4.3 percent, Singapore's 10.7 percent, Taiwan's 10.1 percent and South Korea's 12.2 percent.
The region mainly suffered from the slowdown in the electronics sector, he said.
On the import side, Singson said "it is hard to conclude that developments are symptomatic of an unsustainable demand syndrome."
Imports, which expanded by 26 percent in the first half, was fueled by the ongoing large-scale investments especially in export-oriented and newly liberalised sectors, the central bank chief said.

Moreover, he said "the market understands fully well financing the trade deficit is not a major problem at this stage considering our very large overseas workers remittances and significant inflows of foreign investments."

On the almost static movement of the peso to the dollar, Singson said "this is a current feature of the economy that has been clearly appreciated by investors, business people and by all who need to plan ahead and make longer-term commitments."
